title: The Premier League is back: welcome to the new era of post-verdict unreality | Premier League | The Guardian
description: As the top flight returns, armed with the knowledge its serial champions have been the authors of a 10-year sham supremacy, the first question is simple: how is it going to feel?
Author: Barney Ronay
Headline: As the top flight returns, armed with the knowledge its serial champions have been the authors of a 10-year sham supremacy, the first question is simple: how is it going to feel?
Content: It’s a strange new dawn for Manchester City – and everyone else.Illustration: Guardian Design; Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenIt’s a strange new dawn for Manchester City – and everyone else.Illustration: Guardian Design; Getty ImagesPremier LeagueThe Premier League is back: welcome to the new era of post-verdict unrealityBarney RonayAs the top flight returns, armed with the knowledge its serial champions have been the authors of a 10-year sham supremacy, the first question is simple: how is it going to feel?Fri 9 Oct 2026 15.00 EDTShareThe internet: an apology. It turns out you were right. It was actually a simulation all along. Now, talk to me about chemtrails again. And yes, maybe Vinícius Júniorhasbeen replaced by a handsome, baffled-looking waxwork.Welcome to the weirdest weekend of them all. We are now post-judgment, post-statement, postlapsarian. As the Premier League prepares to snap back into what must be described, out of habit, as reality, armed with the knowledge its serial champions have been the authors ofa 10-year sham supremacy, the first question is fairly simple. How is it going to feel?Maresca refuses to confirm he will stay at Manchester City if club lose appealRead moreThere is no precedent for this. Even the state of total confusion feels brittle given City maintain their complete state of innocence and deny all charges. We await the release of Irrefutable Body of Evidence, the great lost Madonna erotic thriller sequel, presumably recast around a steamy three-year regulatory tribunal scenario.City’s appeal defence appears to be based around the government giving them money. This may or may not be related to how you control what the high court considers admissible. But it is also implied confirmation that the club is the propaganda tool of an overseas state, that Kyle Walker, for example, has basically been a civil servant all these years. Maybe the United Arab Emirates should have six stars on the national team jersey, one for each title. They even look like asterisks.Beyond this there is the more basic issue of how to present this spectacle as entertainment. How do you structure a Match of the Day now? What’s the balance in the edit of bus-rage, taunting banner clips, managerial evasiveness content, versus the trivial stuff on the pitch with the balls and goals and men in shorts?Mainly theManchester Cityaffair has created an existential problem. The key questions in English football are no longer things such aswho will win the league, orwill Tottenham get relegated(although this is still an excellent question). They are instead: what is real now? What was real then? What will be real in the future? Will something that seems real now become unreal later?View image in fullscreenWas Kyle Walker basically a civil servant during his time at City?Photograph: Carl Recine/Getty ImagesThe whole experience brings to mind visiting the Yas Marina Formula One track in Abu Dhabi a few years back, a pristine place, all sweeping curves, perfect surfaces, dreamy floral boulevards. At that stage exploring its far reaches, following the curve around the final corner, led to: nothing. Out of sight the hanging baskets stopped dead. The sprinklers cut out. The pavement ended. The next step took you straight into sand and dead space.Beyond the main stage the Yas track was a set, an imitation of life. And it turns out this is basically what Abu Dhabi was doing to thePremier Leaguein the years 2009 to 2018: creating a product, a simulacrum, a pop-up.At the end of which we have a blurring of edges, different versions of what could be real eliding into one another, a place where an AI video of Uncle Phil from the Fresh Prince scoring the Özil goal against Ludogorets seems just as real, just as plausible asCity’s 6-0 thrashing of Watfordin the FA Cup final. Seen through that lens this can feel like an extinction-level problem. Being real is, in the end, all sport actually has.It feels fitting City’s first date in the new unreality is Liverpool at Anfield on Sunday, one of the great Premier League fixtures recast as a kind of ceremonial shame-event, a requiem for a dream. Liverpool have a clearer sense of grievance than most, having been deprived of league titles three times on the final day by a club that was colouring outside the lines.In many ways the game at Anfield is a perfect snapshot of what we have lost. This should be an entirely pure and gripping sporting contest. Instead the biggest story in top-tier English football is the meaninglessness of top-tier English football. The headline product is gossip, side-eye, legal backstory.In their next 14 league games City will play three teams who have reserved the right to sue them. How can these occasions be seen as credible acts of sport? Even the banter-culture is out of date. For the past 12 years City at Anfield has been soundtracked by theSteve Gerrard/He slipped on his arseincident, a source of public pain that has defined the late-stage career of Liverpool’s most beloved modern captain. Except, we now know the actual story is the club that finished above them were cheating.View image in fullscreenSteven Gerrard afterthatmistake against Chelsea in 2014.Photograph: Peter Byrne/PAIt turns out this is the first stage of football grief. Poring over the endless counterfactuals. Some are pretty stark. The five league titles won on the last day of the season. The1-0 FA Cup final victory against Stoke, coached by a man with two contracts, the winning goal scored by a player linked, by close association, with the book-cooking regime.There is a butterfly effect here of endless interference. What do Inter make of all this? Imaginelosing a Champions League finalthat could have transformed your modern history, by the narrowest margin, to a club that appear to have built their own era out of cheating on their income. Two years later Inter were thrashed byanother nation-state teamand Simone Inzaghi was shunted off the set. He’s in Saudi now. Just get on the train.Then there’s the wider structural stuff. City spent nine years flooding the zone with government-backed transfer funds (€1.2bn in those nine years: miles out in front), skewing the money supply in every league in Europe. The extra £20m disbursed at the last moment to drag Kevin De Bruyne out of the Bundesliga. What happens if that doesn’t happen?At home, Spurs missed the Champions League by one spot four times, always in City’s slipstream. Would Manchester United have signed Rasmus Højlund without that steamrollering model of Erling Haaland-era success?How to reprocess the deep cultural influence of Pep Guardiola? This was based on Guardiola’s genius as a coach, which is still real, irrespective of the gradient of the playing field. But nothing succeeds like success. Winners get to rewrite history. How does it feel now that Guardiola’s style affected so profoundly the way kids play park football, the way young coaches work, all of it based on sustained blockbusting example?Even the Football Association’s England DNA pathway was basically a Pep document, predicated on the undeniable evidence of his winning way. The method is still good, the detail unarguable, the tactical blueprint pure. But that 10-year spell in England was also supercharged by cheating.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionWe mourn too the legend of the Catalan brain trust, the hours spent studying this pure and monk-like dynamic. Yeah, fine. But also chuck vast amounts of hidden cash at it. Not to mention the hundreds of articles, podcasts, academic studies, fan tributes and personal tomes about purity, legacy, style, the glory that sailed above all other questions.View image in fullscreenPep Guardiola reminds Liverpool fans of his six titles in 2024, but how now do we assess his influence?Photograph: Ian Hodgson/APCity’s fans are entitled to some space here, a chance to effect their own reckoning up. Elements of that support may have responded over the years with bizarre levels of aggression to any questioning of the process. But it is also normal to believe what you’re told, not least when it includes the profound transformation of the thing you love. How to process a total narrative U-turn?The City documentary series A Beautiful Obsession is a far more interesting watch now, like The Sixth Sense when you know the ending. The project is cast by its editors as a pure passion play, Pep portrayed as a tunnel-vision obsessive, pictured most often staring at a whiteboard covered in magnets while the world turns beyond his line of vision.It is impossible now not to see some kind of willed seclusion, Prospero on his island, rough magic starting to fray as reality crashes on to the shores. Episodes one to four are portrayed as a Viking funeral for the age of Pep. But they are now an unwitting farewell to something else too. In his final appearance Pep is shown quoting Kipling, saying triumph and disaster are both impostors. And he’s right. It turns out they were. Most notably the triumph bits.Just before the end credits we see one of City’s club channel celebrations, with boards plastered in the usual phrases the club seems to feel drawn to. This is how it felt. We see things they’ll never see. Looking back this was always part of the dynamic, the insistence, which is usually just taken as read, that this is all real, that the feelings were feelings, that nobody can fake this away.It is still the mantra for some. And maybe that’s true. But if so, what did it add up to in the first place? An episode of a TV show? An induced high, a snort of disposable pleasure?View image in fullscreenManchester City fans celebrate their 2012 Premier League title. They too are entitled to some space here.Photograph: Tom Jenkins/Getty ImagesBut then, this is also not the end. There is always disasterism in football, the sense the thing happening now is the thing that will always happen. But football’s enduring strength, the one thing that marks it out as indestructible, is its relentlessness. We are in the period of rupture and parallax error. But how long will it last?Plenty of good can still come from this. The idea that English football is profoundly damaged by this may prove wide of the mark. What is happening here, and this includes the outcome of the appeal, is that rules are being enforced. Andy Burnham may have confused the process with histone-deaf and weirdly partial comments. But for all the delay and indecision this is still the rule of law in action.And maybe English football gets to learn something. Maybe the unregulated nature of the league can reset a little. At the very least it seems axiomatic the new regulatory powers should ensure no nation state, or state fund, however you want to semanticise it, gets to own a club again.There are still 33 rounds of Premier League games to run in the age of whiplash. The current interlude may feel like a football version of those bits in the Terminator films where Sarah Connor drives around in a Jeep looking glazed and distant, prepping for the time of skulls and robot death-rays, disengaged from the meaningless lives of blind and foolish humans.Football always moves on. Throw flares at a bus, taunt the deceived souls in the away end. But the future is still wide open. Perhaps we can even face it with a little hope in the time of conflict.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueManchester CitycommentShareReuse this content

title: Bucky Irving runs riot as Buccaneers stun Cowboys for first win of season | NFL | The Guardian
description: Bucky Irving rushed for a career-high 165 yards and scored twice as Tampa Bay capitalized on Dallas mistakes to claim a surprise 24-16 victory
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: Bucky Irving rushed for a career-high 165 yards and scored twice as Tampa Bay capitalized on Dallas mistakes to claim a surprise 24-16 victory
Content: Tampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Jalon Daniels celebrates a touchdown during the first half of Thursday night’s 24-16 win over the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas.Photograph: Stacy Revere/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenTampa Bay Buccaneers quarterback Jalon Daniels celebrates a touchdown during the first half of Thursday night’s 24-16 win over the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas.Photograph: Stacy Revere/Getty ImagesNFLBucky Irving runs riot as Buccaneers stun Cowboys for first win of seasonIrving rushes for career-high 165 yards and two TDsRookie Daniels impresses in second NFL startPrescott throws two picks as Dallas fall to 2-3AgenciesThu 8 Oct 2026 23.44 EDTLast modified on Fri 9 Oct 2026 10.49 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleBucky Irving already had his first 100-yard game since his rookie year in 2024 when the Tampa Bay running back finished off theDallas Cowboyswith a run that gave him a career high.Jalon Daniels, the undrafted rookie filling in for franchise quarterback Baker Mayfield, enjoyed the view while doing plenty himself to get the Buccaneers their first win of the season in just his second start.Irving ran for 165 yards, including a 72-yard run to set up the touchdown that put Tampa Bay ahead for good while scoring twice himself, and the Buccaneers beat the Cowboys 24-16 on Thursday night.Daniels threw a TD pass to Irving in the first half while directing a turnover-free offense and amid several Dallas miscues, finishing an efficient 19 of 25 for 189 yards as the Bucs piled up 241 yards rushing.Daniels is filling in for Mayfield, who’s expected to be sidelined at least one more game with a dislocated thumb on his throwing hand.“Six months ago, if you would have told me that my first win would have been on a Thursday night, [Amazon] Prime football game, I don’t know what I would have told you,” said Daniels, who threw three interceptions in a 17-14 loss to Green Bay in his debut. “Like I keep saying, through all the highs and lows, the bads, the goods, go through every single emotion because at the end of the day, it makes you better and prepares you for any situation that comes down the line.”Irving had 21 carries and a 7.9-yard average while scoring on a five-yard pass and a one-yard plunge as the Bucs (1-4) finally found some footing in a season that started with expectations of winning the NFC South.View image in fullscreenBuccaneers running back Bucky Irving breaks past Cowboys linebacker Dee Winters during the second half of Thursday night’s 24-16 win at AT&T Stadium.Photograph: Julio Cortez/AP“We lost the first quarter of the season,” Bucs coach Todd Bowles said. “We didn’t lose the second, third or fourth. We’ve still got to play those. So we started the second quarter tonight. It’s a long way to climb out, but at the same time, we’re upbeat and if we played as hard and played as effective, we’ll be OK.”Dak Prescott led a 99-yard drive and threw a 13-yard TD pass to George Pickens in the fourth quarter before his second interception off a tipped pass helped Tampa Bay clinch the win in the final two minutes.The Cowboys (2-3) continued an up-and-down start to the season, this time with an offense that was at times as sloppy as the defense has been in both seasons under coach Brian Schottenheimer.“I didn’t plan on being 2-3, disappointed by that for sure,” Schottenheimer said. “But we’re just getting started. There’s a lot of football left and we’re gonna play better. We know that.”After Irving’s long run on the first play of the second half was followed by receiver Emeka Egbuka’s 14-yard TD run on a jet sweep, Prescott threw his first interception and the Dallas defense left Tez Johnson wide open on a 64-yard grab that led to Irving’s one-yard plunge for a 21-10 lead.KaVontae Turpin’s fumble on the subsequent kickoff led to a Tampa Bay field goal, but only after the Bucs converted a third-and-21 from the Dallas 48-yard line with Daniels’s 21-yard pass to Egbuka.The Cowboys were missing one of the pieces they recently added to try to fix a porous defense. Cornerback Joey Porter Jr was a late scratch in what was supposed to be his second appearance since arriving in a trade from Pittsburgh last week.Prescott was 24 of 42 for 316 yards in his first two-interception game of the season – his first picks since the opener.Explore more on these topicsNFLDallas CowboysTampa Bay BuccaneersUS sportsShareReuse this content

title: Wolff tells critics to ‘watch Teletubbies or Mickey Mouse not F1’ as he defends Mercedes’ strategy | Mercedes GP | The Guardian
description: Toto Wolff has condemned accusations of bias in how he has managed George Russell and Kimi Antonelli, describing those making the claims as better off watching ‘Teletubbies or Mickey Mouse’ rather than F1
Author: Giles Richards
Headline: Toto Wolff has condemned accusations of bias in how he has managed George Russell and Kimi Antonelli, describing those making the claims as better off watching ‘Teletubbies or Mickey Mouse’ rather than F1
Content: George Russell in sprint qualifying at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, where he took second on the grid.Photograph: Vincent Thian/APView image in fullscreenGeorge Russell in sprint qualifying at the Marina Bay Street Circuit, where he took second on the grid.Photograph: Vincent Thian/APMercedes GPWolff tells critics to ‘watch Teletubbies or Mickey Mouse not F1’ as he defends Mercedes’ strategyPrincipal denies bias towards Antonelli over RussellVerstappen takes pole in sprint qualifying in SingaporeGiles RichardsFri 9 Oct 2026 12.42 EDTLast modified on Fri 9 Oct 2026 13.11 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleToto Wolff has condemned accusations of bias in how he has managed his drivers George Russell andKimi Antonelli, with the Mercedes team principal describing those positing such theories as better off watching “Teletubbies or Mickey Mouse” rather than Formula One.With Antonelli leading Russell by 84 points in the world championship as they go into this weekend’s Singapore Grand Prix, the Italian’s first title is within his reach. The 20-year-old has driven superbly in only his second season in F1 but Russell has struggled with poor fortune and reliability issues that have stymied his championship challenge.Valtteri Bottas reveals lizard-leaping, python-dodging cycling exploits on epic rideRead moreAt thelast round, in Malaysia, an engine failure cost Russell a potential podium spot and led to a host of accusations online of bias towards Antonelli. Speaking in Singapore, Wolff’s exasperation was clear.“They’re brainless, whoever thinks that, it’s completely nonsensical,” he said. “I don’t know what’s going on. Do they think I have a button that says: ‘George, engine failure now’? Or disadvantaging one driver against the other when we are fighting for a constructors’ championship when we have always had the mindset of providing everybody equal material?“There’s a lot of polarisation and sometimes I read what people write. I find it hilarious. These people really contribute to my own entertainment when they are abusing the team or myself. I’m Satan, I’ve heard. So, overall funny. But really, zero understanding and respect for people who come up with these things. Rather than watchingFormula One, they should do Teletubbies or some Mickey Mouse.”Russell goes into Sunday’s night race on the Marina Bay circuit clinging on in the title fight. Not only did the engine failure cost him in Malaysia but it meant he has had to take a new engine for this race and with the attendant penalties will have to start from the back of the grid on a track where overtaking is enormously tricky.View image in fullscreenToto Wolff and his Mercedes team have been grappling with engine troubles this week.Photograph: Sam Bloxham/LAT ImagesMercedes have further complications in Singapore. The upgrades they brought to Malaysia did not prove effective and have left the team somewhat perplexed as to why they had not delivered. They opted, with Russell’s approval, to split their options this weekend with the British driver reverting to the spec with which he hadwon in Bakuand Antonelli running the new version in order to provide an insight into where the developments were wanting.In qualifying for Saturday’s sprint race, Russell was clearly enjoying his pre-upgrade ride more than his teammate. He took second on the grid with Antonelli only in seventh, while Max Verstappen took an excellent pole to back up his win at Sepang. Antonelli certainly felt he was somewhat under the cosh in Singapore with a car far removed from what he is used to. “There is still a lot to understand about this package, the car is very difficult, very unpredictable,” he said. “I was coming in with high hopes but so far it has been very difficult. It’s going to be a difficult weekend, it’s going to be very tricky. I don’t see where we can find seven-tenths.”Mercedes are clear they will continue to allow their drivers to race one another. Wolff, who managed three seasons of increasingly intense and rancorous rivalry between Lewis Hamilton and Nico Rosberg between 2014 and 2016, has always been insistent that he has practised even-handed management since he joined F1. He cited a conversation he had with Alain Prost about his bitter rivalry with Ayrton Senna while at McLaren in the 1980s.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toThe RecapThe best of our sports journalism from the past seven days and a heads-up on the weekend’s actionEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotion“I remember being a complete rookie and running into Alain Prost on the grid of a race and I said: ‘Why did it go so wrong between you and Senna?’ He said: ‘Because we never knew what the team was about. You felt that you were the flavour of the month one time and then two months later you thought the politics were going against you. There were different situations where you had the feeling that you’re really not wanted.’“So, I took it as my challenge to keep it always balanced and it was not easy with Lewis and Nico back in the day. That’s why people can think what they want but the integrity in that respect is something that’s important for me, and the drivers know it.”Russell has admitted Antonelli has done a better job overall this season, while also noting that he would have expected to still be in the fight were it not for some of the problems he has suffered. He looked quick on the Marina Bay circuit on Friday but still has a huge task to come through the field on Sunday.Antonelli’s advantage is such that if he is 101 points ahead after this meeting, he could become F1’s youngest world champion at the next round in Austin. A title, as Wolff would doubtless attest, that will have been won purely on merit.Explore more on these topicsMercedes GPGeorge RussellKimi AntonelliToto WolffFormula One 2026Formula OneMotor sportnewsShareReuse this content

title: Zavier Gozo: ‘You have to be uncomfortable to get to the highest levels’ | Crystal Palace | The Guardian
description: Crystal Palace’s American import had never lived anywhere but Utah before moving to London. Now, he’s aiming for more Premier League minutes
Author: Jeff Rueter
Headline: Crystal Palace’s American import had never lived anywhere but Utah before moving to London. Now, he’s aiming for more Premier League minutes
Content: Zavier Gozo has made three appearances for Crystal Palace.Photograph: Sebastian Frej/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenZavier Gozo has made three appearances for Crystal Palace.Photograph: Sebastian Frej/Getty ImagesCrystal PalaceInterviewZavier Gozo: ‘You have to be uncomfortable to get to the highest levels’Jeff RueterCrystal Palace’s American import had never lived anywhere but Utah before moving to London. Now, he’s aiming for more Premier League minutesFri 9 Oct 2026 05.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 9 Oct 2026 11.41 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleMuch has changed in Zavier Gozo’s life since May.Back then, Gozo was a day removed from learning he wasn’t among Mauricio Pochettino’s 26 selections for the World Cup, having just made what proved to be his third-to-last appearance with boyhood club Real Salt Lake.Gozo had only ever lived in Utah at that point. He would watch the World Cup from home, where he lived with his mother.Today, less than five months later, he lives half a world away. He is gettingPremier Leagueminutes and, as of a week ago, made his first appearance for the senior US men’s national team.“It’s a big change to go from Utah to London,” said this master of understatement, stationed on a sofa in the lobby of the US team’s downtown Minneapolis hotel in shorts, slippers and a pristine white hoodie.With no Pulisic and good results, have the USMNT moved on from their savior complex? | Leander SchaerlaeckensRead moreHe has joined a familiar face at Crystal Palace, at least, in his new international teammate – Chris Richards. The center-back has become a stalwart for club and country since joining Palace in 2022. He’s an every-minute option along the back line, arguably their lead defender after the recent exits of Marc Guéhi and Maxence Lacroix. Gozo hasevidently endeared himselfto Richards’s toddler daughter, too.Then again, landing alongside a compatriot was far from the biggest hook that helped Gozo opt for Palace.“I think I knew more [about them] than maybe the average [club],” Gozo says before listing their recent triumphs in the FA Cup, the Community Shield (both in 2025) and the Conference League (in 2026). “They were in a good run of form, and they have been for the last couple years, and have been showing it on the European stage.“I’ve known them from [Wilfried] Zaha, and being a very good club that develops wingers and forwards in general. It seems like they always have a player that’s coming through their system that’s either sold for a lot or just becomes a very good player. And obviously, when Chris was there, I was just following them, and him, and their success. I feel like I knew a fair amount.”Given Gozo’s ambitions, Palace’s track record of developing both players from their own academy and those brought in from other clubs was a significant reassurance. Their trophy cabinet and its rapidly waning open shelving was another boost, and a place in the Europa League this season offered even more games for Gozo to make his mark.By the end of his time in MLS, Gozo hardly showed a flicker of fear. On one occasion, against Atlanta, he collected a ball at the edge of the final third near the right touchline with minimal attacking support. Rather than wait for support, he swiftly put the defender marking him through the spin cycle, cleverly dribbling infield anduncorking a curlerto the far post. Four weeks later, against Kansas City, a split-second at the edge of the box was all he needed toexecute a bombastic self-volley.Rather than taking an incremental step up in difficulty, he’s now contending to make the bench in the world’s most competitive league.“I think the coaching staff believes in me and is bought into developing me and the talent that I have,” Gozo said. “I think it’s a perfect environment for me to learn, but also be thrown into the fire a little bit. When you’re at RSL and you’re starting to become their best player, or one of their best players, and you go toCrystal Palace, sometimes you can lose confidence. Because it’s like, ‘Oh wow, I can’t do the things I used to be able to do.’“You just kind of have to figure out how you can become effective again, and yeah, obviously it can be hard at times, but also it’s what you want. You have to be uncomfortable to get to the highest levels.”skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Twice weeklySign up toSoccer DeskJonathan Wilson and Guardian journalists bring expert analysis and reporting on the biggest stories in soccer.Enter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionGone are the days of being the boy wonder, the homegrown hero fans watched develop into a leading forward inMLS. Now Gozo bears the pressure that comes with arriving on an eight-figure transfer fee, one of many promising American upstarts determined to thrive at the sport’s highest levels.“It’s very different. Obviously, you don’t feel the connection with the fans as much. But also, you want to be able to do something for the fans, for them to be able to connect with you,” Gozo said. “[You want to] bring them happiness and bring them joy with what you do on the field. It’s more trying to prove yourself to the fans; I feel like with the fans of RSL, it’s kind of like they’re bringing you up, like giving you confidence while you’re coming up.”He’s made three appearances from the bench for Palace in all competitions thus far, giving him a sense of the newly raised bar. The rate of play has increased considerably. Those defenders meeting him on the wing, like the aforementioned poor soul in Atlanta, are better supported by their teammates. Those spaces at the edge of the box, like the plot of grass afforded to him by Kansas City, are in far shorter supply.For now, anyway.View image in fullscreenZavier Gozo made his international debut in the last international window.Photograph: Mark Thorstenson/ISI Photos/Getty ImagesAsked what he aims to improve after his Premier League introduction, Gozo said “physicality and not even being necessarily strong, but using your body in a way to either win a foul or protect the ball, and knowing when to take two touches, or take one touch, or turn and go dribble. Those are all things that you just have to have kind of perfect.”Further refining those skills should also help him stick around Pochettino’s rejuvenated USMNT project. This past international window saw Gozo debut along with 12 rising upstarts, including fellow wingers Cavan Sullivan and Mathis Albert. Gozo appeared in just one of the four friendlies, logging nearly half an hour against Peru.Gozo may be new to the senior team, but past camps and tournaments at the youth international levels are especially relevant given the program’s young sea change. He was one of five members from the 2025 U-20 World Cup squad to debut this window, having played with some since his first call-up to the U-15 level in 2022.“I feel like the vibe at the national team has changed, especially since Pochettino has come here,” Gozo said, “Even just since the World Cup, I think a lot of people are more involved and paying attention.… It’s just an elevated energy, almost. It feels good to walk in and to be a part of this group.”Explore more on these topicsCrystal PalaceMLSReal Salt LakePremier LeagueUSAUS sportsinterviewsShareReuse this content

title: LeBron James shines in pre-season debut for revamped Philadelphia 76ers | Philadelphia 76ers | The Guardian
description: The 41-year-old scored 10 points and added five assists in his first outing for the Sixers, who fell 114-108 to Brooklyn
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The 41-year-old scored 10 points and added five assists in his first outing for the Sixers, who fell 114-108 to Brooklyn
Content: LeBron James and Tyrese Maxey of the Philadelphia 76ers talk during Thursday night’s pre-season game against the Brooklyn Nets at Barclays Center in New York.Photograph: Jesse D Garrabrant/NBAE/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenLeBron James and Tyrese Maxey of the Philadelphia 76ers talk during Thursday night’s pre-season game against the Brooklyn Nets at Barclays Center in New York.Photograph: Jesse D Garrabrant/NBAE/Getty ImagesPhiladelphia 76ersLeBron James shines in pre-season debut for revamped Philadelphia 76ersJames scores 10 points in 18-minute Sixers debutJaylen Brown leads Philadelphia with 18 pointsNets pull away in third quarter for 114-108 victoryAgenciesThu 8 Oct 2026 23.29 EDTLast modified on Fri 9 Oct 2026 11.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleNBA superstar LeBron James delivered a solid first-half performance in his first pre-season game for Philadelphia on Thursday, but the new-look 76ers fell 114-108 to theBrooklyn Nets.James, the NBA’s all-time leading scorer, announced in July that he had signed atwo-year, $8m dealwith the 76ers, ending weeks of speculation over where the four-time NBA champion would land as a free agent after eight seasons and one title with the Los Angeles Lakers.The 41-year-old, entering a record-extending 24thNBAseason, won two titles with Miami, another with Cleveland and a fourth with the Lakers. He is aiming to help the Sixers win their first championship since Julius Erving led the team to the title in 1983.Thursday’s game marked his first chance to play alongside new teammates Joel Embiid, VJ Edgecombe, Tyrese Maxey and Jaylen Brown, who arrived from the Boston Celtics.James scored 10 points, making his only shot from the field and all eight of his free-throw attempts. He added four rebounds, five assists and a steal in 18 minutes and four seconds, all in the first half.Brown led all scorers with 18 points. Julius Randle had 14 for the Nets, who outscored the Sixers 37-23 in the third quarter to take control.But all eyes were on James, starting with his signature pre-game chalk toss, performed for the first time in a 76ers uniform.James smoothly directed the Sixers’ offense during his time on the floor, recording all five of his assists in the first quarter and combining effectively with Maxey.View image in fullscreenLeBron James performs his signature pre-game chalk toss before making his Philadelphia 76ers debut against the Brooklyn Nets on Thursday night at Barclays Center.Photograph: Jesse D Garrabrant/NBAE/Getty Images“I think there was some really good things happening, you know, right off the bat,” 76ers coach Nick Nurse said after seeing his starters together for the first time.“A bunch of back cuts and good passing et cetera ... there were segments where obviously we turned the ball over a lot ... just the little clunky segments, too. But, again, it’s pre-season, first time they’re together.“I think you look at it as what’s good and what are the learning experiences, things that we can improve.”The 76ers have two more pre-season games, both against Boston, before opening the regular season against the defending champion New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden on 20 October.James’s arrival has already left the 76ers contending with distractions away from the court.The superstar took to Instagram to dispute a claim made by a play-by-play announcer during the team’s first pre-season game on Monday that he had admonished Embiid for arriving late to practice.“He ain’t been late, so stop the lie,” James posted.James acknowledged at the team’s media day last month that the attention surrounding the 76ers would be “doubled, tripled and quadrupled now that I’m here”.Explore more on these topicsPhiladelphia 76ersLeBron JamesUS sportsNBABrooklyn NetsShareReuse this content

title: Lionesses take control of World Cup playoff tie but unfancied Greece still in fight | Women's World Cup 2027 qualifiers | The Guardian
description: Georgia Stanway, Maya Le Tissier and Alessia Russo were on target as England earned a 3-1 win away to Greece in the first leg of their World Cup playoff
Author: Tom Garry
Headline: Georgia Stanway, Maya Le Tissier and Alessia Russo were on target as England earned a 3-1 win away to Greece in the first leg of their World Cup playoff
Content: Alessia Russo reacts after scoring England’s third goal against Greece.Photograph: Alex Davidson/Uefa/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenAlessia Russo reacts after scoring England’s third goal against Greece.Photograph: Alex Davidson/Uefa/Getty ImagesWomen's World Cup 2027 qualifiersLionesses take control of World Cup playoff tie but unfancied Greece still in fightWorld Cup qualifying playoff: Greece 1-3 EnglandStanway, Le Tissier and Russo on targetTom Garryat the Stadio PankritioFri 9 Oct 2026 14.46 EDTLast modified on Fri 9 Oct 2026 19.01 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleSarina Wiegman said she wanted to see a bit more from her side after their fairly underwhelming performance against a hugely unfancied Greek side, despite securing a valuable first-leg victory in their Women’s World Cup playoff tie.Georgia Stanway’s neat finish, Maya Le Tissier’s first England goal and Alessia Russo’s low strike were enough to give England control but a Kallisti Brouksair goal for Greece means that the tie is not definitively over, going into Tuesday’s second leg, and Wiegman acknowledged that England had been “a bit sloppy” at times.“I think we made it a bit harder [for ourselves],” Wiegman said, while also giving credit to Greece for being “very well-prepared, very well-organised and very disciplined”, before adding: “Of course, I’m happy with the 3-1. I’m not happy with the 1.“We were – in moments – really good on the ball, and we were, in moments, not so good on the ball and we could have made better decisions, too.Russo’s return to form is vital but Lionesses still lack bite against low blocks | Suzanne WrackRead more“We want to play really well. Of course, we go out to win, but we want to show more than winning, we want to play really well too.”Facing a Greek side ranked 59th in the world, who have never qualified for a major tournament, England began as overwhelming favourites and dominated the ball but often appeared to be going through the motions, making hard work of breaking down Greece’s deep defensive shape. It would be too much of a stretch to describe it as a bad performance but, at the same time, England did lack their usual zip, charisma and urgency and their body language suggested they were focused on the job at hand, rather than enjoying themselves.Perhaps the flat atmosphere was to blame for that. The Hellenic Football Federation had made the tickets free for this fixture but – despite that – only a few thousand turned up and there was scarcely any cheers from the home supporters. Instead, around 500 travelling England fans were generating the majority of the noise.It meant that the first 45 minutes were largely forgettable and lacking in real quality, aside from a few isolated moments such as a delicious chip from 25 yards out from Lauren James, which drew a gasp of appreciation from the away fans as it hit the net and they thought England had taken the lead. A VAR check showed that James was offside.View image in fullscreenGeorgia Stanway finishes off an England team move to open the scoring in Greece.Photograph: Miloš Bičanski/Getty ImagesEngland were playing with a back three when in possession, pushing Le Tissier very high up the pitch as a right wing-back, and with a back four when out of possession. They were untroubled defensively except for a huge let-off at 0-0 when the Greece striker Ionna Papatheodorou hit the woodwork. She eased past Esme Morgan and Leah Williamson with alarming ease and her shot from range looked to have beaten Hannah Hampton, but struck the bar.England, who had gone close when Laura Blindkilde Brown shot straight at the goalkeeper, James curled a free-kick wide and Lauren Hemp drilled a low shot narrowly wide across the face of goal, eventually found their breakthrough when Blindkilde Brown played a quick ball to Russo, whose good touch to lay the ball off for Stanway allowed the midfielder to slot in low.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |WeeklySign up toMoving the GoalpostsNo topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionAfter the break, Le Tissier powered in a strong finish after clever work from Keira Walsh to open up space, and when Russo tucked a low finish into the bottom corner to make it 3-0 four minutes later, England might have been hoping the floodgates were open. However, some limp defending allowed Rangers’ Brouksair to pull a goal back, firing in a low finish after a hopeful, bouncing, high long ball was not initially dealt with by Morgan.Quick GuideWomen's World Cup qualifying roundupShowTheRepublic of Irelandcruised to an 8-0 victory in the first leg of their Women’s World Cup qualifying play-off againstKazakhstanin Astana. Kyra Carusa scored twice while further goals from Chloe Mustaki, Emily Murphy, Abbie Larkin, Jamie Finn, Shanade Hopcroft and Jessie Stapleton made Tuesday’s second leg in Cork a formality. Carusa had already grabbed her brace – and Mustaki also hit the target – before the Kazakhstan captain, Yulia Myasnikova, was sent off just beyond the half-hour mark for a foul on Larkin. The decision allowed the visitors to shrug off the absence of Katie McCabe due to injury and stroll to victory, with the outstanding Mustaki providing the assists for both Carusa’s goals as well as the fifth for Larkin shortly before half-time.ScotlanddefeatedCzechia2-0 in Pardubice, with Caroline Weir and Claire Emslie on target in the second half. Tereza Krejciríkova was sent off for the hosts three minutes from time. A 21st-minute Ezmiralda Franja own goal securedWalesa 1-0 win inAlbania.Northern Ireland's World Cup hopes are all but over, however, after a 4-0 first leg home loss byPortugal. Telma Encarnação, Jéssica Silva, a Rebecca Holloway own goal and Fátima Pinto the scorers.Was this helpful?Thank you for your feedback.England went close to adding to their tally, as James curled narrowly wide and the substitute Jess Park’s effort hit the bar, on a night when Erica Meg Parkinson and Grace Fisk were handed senior international debuts, late on.Assuming they finish the job off on Tuesday in the second leg in Leicester, England would face Slovakia or Ukraine in the second round of the playoffs in the November-December international window. That tie would also be staged over two legs and England would need to win that to secure their spot at next summer’s tournament in Brazil. To be competitive there, though, they know they will need to markedly improve on their cohesion and fluidity with the ball.Wiegman said: “I have seen some fluid moments too. You just want more. And you want the final balls and the positions in front of the goal [to be] better, and of course we’re working on that, with the amount of time we have. Some things, we’d really want to do better and we’re working really hard to do so. We have an opportunity now to fix that, for Tuesday.”Explore more on these topicsWomen's World Cup 2027 qualifiersEngland women's football teamWomen's footballmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Managers react to Manchester City’s guilty verdict: ‘Uncertainty is not good for anyone’ | Manchester City | The Guardian
description: United manager Carrick rues missing out on ‘emotion in the moment’ while Iraola says he understands why Liverpool fans are angry
Author: Guardian sport
Headline: United manager Carrick rues missing out on ‘emotion in the moment’ while Iraola says he understands why Liverpool fans are angry
Content: Liverpool head coach Andoni Iraola during training on Thursday.Photograph: Andrew Powell/Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenLiverpool head coach Andoni Iraola during training on Thursday.Photograph: Andrew Powell/Liverpool FC/Getty ImagesThe talkManchester CityManagers react to Manchester City’s guilty verdict: ‘Uncertainty is not good for anyone’United manager Carrick rues missing out on ‘emotion in the moment’ while Iraola says he understands why Liverpool fans are angryGuardian sportFri 9 Oct 2026 17.30 EDTFirst published on Fri 9 Oct 2026 11.06 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on Google1.Carrick ‘personally’ affected by verdictMichael Carrick has said retrospectively receiving a winner’s medal would not make up for being robbed of emotional moments of glory by Manchester City’s breaches of the Premier League’s financial rules.Manchester United’s manager was part of the squad that lost out on the Premier League title to City on the final day of the 2011-12 season whenSergio Agüero scored a last-minute winnerto secure top spot on goal difference. Carrick and his United teammates were left solemn on the touchline at Sunderland while City, who have been found guilty of breaking financial rules during a nine-year-period between 2009 and 2018, celebrated.“The emotion, the feeling about winning, a lot of it is in the moment,” Carrick said. “Whether you’re successful, whether you lose, whether it goes against you, that initial [feeling], the beauty of sport and the beauty of football and the beauty of trying to win trophies here, is a little bit on the journey towards it and then the finale, and does it go for you, does it go against you.“Once that’s done, there’s no getting that back in any direction. The feeling we all crave is coming out on top – that kind of sums it up. Whatever’s done in the past tense is in the past, but in that moment is how you feel in that moment. Certainly as a participant, as a performer, and I’m sure the supporters feel the same, that’s why we love it so much because of the emotion in the moment.”Carrick was also part of United’s staff under Ole Gunnar Solskjær when they finished second, 22 points behind City, in 2021. City continue to plead their innocence and have appealed against the verdict. If they fail to overturn the independent commission’s ruling, they will probably face a serious punishment.“It’s affected me personally in different ways,” Carrick said. “But as the case is ongoing now I don’t know where that stands and how it’s going to end up, so we’ll just have to wait and see. What I will say, the sooner it gets sorted I think for everyone’s benefit is essential.”Will Unwin2.Iraola understands Liverpool fan angerAndoni Iraola understands the anger among Liverpool supporters towards Manchester City and believes the Premier League needs a resolution to the scandal engulfing English football as swiftly as possible.Iraola avoided condemning City during his first press conference since the club were found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules on an industrial scale over nine years. City have lodged an appeal against the findings and Liverpool’s head coach admitted a final, definitive verdict is essential for the good of the game. “I think it should be [concluded quickly],” he said. “There should be a moment when something comes from this, but now is not that moment. Nobody knows what is going to happen and I think this uncertainty is no good for anyone.”While refusing to be drawn on the controversy while the legal process is ongoing, Iraola acknowledged the strength of feeling that will be directed at City by Liverpool fans at Anfield on Sunday. City pipped Liverpool to the Premier League title in 2013-14, 2018-19 and 2021-22, the latter two during the fierce rivalry that developed between Jürgen Klopp’s and Pep Guardiola’s teams. Sunday’s reception for the current league leaders promises to be brutal.“We understand and I understand everything that goes above football,” said Iraola. “Every fan will have their own opinion and attitude towards that but it’s not something that I can control. I need to do my job, to give the best game we can give on the sporting side, so everyone of our supporters is happy on Sunday. I think the challenge of the game for us is big.”Liverpool’s task on Sunday, as Iraola referenced, will be complicated by the absence of leading goalscorer Alexander Isak and the in-form Cody Gakpo due to injuries sustained on international duty. The two are not long-term absentees but, with Liverpool facing four games in 10 days, they could miss several matches. He admitted: “It’s a bad thing for us, definitely, because both of them have been prolific at the start of the season but the good thing when you coach Liverpool is you still have very good players available. I trust the players we have ready to go. It’s also a good moment for those players to step up, to add good numbers and good performances while we recover Cody and Alex.”Andy Hunter3.Kompany ‘really proud’ of City medalsVincent Kompany, the former Manchester City captain, insists he is still “really proud” of his success with the club after it was found guilty of breaching Premier League financial rules. The Bayern Munich manager won four Premier League titles and multiple domestic cups during his spell at City from 2008 to 2019.The former Belgium international was a key figure in City’s dominant era under their Abu Dhabi-based owners and is honoured with a statue outside the Etihad Stadium.“I played 11 years for the club. I’ve loved all of the years I played for the club and everything we achieved and [did] on the pitch – that’s something I’m really proud of,” Kompany said.View image in fullscreenA statue of the former Manchester City player Vincent Kompany’s stands outside the Etihad: ‘I’m really proud of everything we achieved.’Photograph: Dave Thompson/APKompany signed for City from Hamburg just weeks before Sheikh Mansour completed a takeover that turned the club from also-rans to serial winners. Asked about the off-pitch issues at his former club, he said: “Everything else, as a player you’re not a part of that and right now as a coach of Bayern Munich I’m not too much occupied with that topic. I’m preparing the game next week and preparing the game we have tomorrow and everything I have as a coach.”Agence France-Presse4.Arteta will wait for judgment before speakingMikel Arteta has insisted his conscience is clear about his time as Manchester City’s assistant manager and promised to “talk with clarity” about his former club when their appeal against a guilty verdict on more than 100 Premier League’s charges has been decided.Arteta spent more than three years as Pep Guardiola’s assistant at City before moving to Arsenal in December 2019. The Spaniard, who signed a lucrative new four-year contract this week, moved to the Etihad in July 2016 and was part of Guardiola’s backroom staff as they won titles in 2018 and 2019.The first came during the period in which City breached financial regulations, according to an independent commission. Arteta was reluctant to discuss any potential punishment City could face but was asked whether his conscience was clear from his spell at City and responded: “Yes.”That was as far as he was prepared to venture after being bombarded with questions about City before Arsenal’s game against Leeds on Saturday. Arteta had been due to deliver a statement at the start of his press conference but the plan changed at the last minute. He refused to be drawn on how he felt when he heard the verdict or whether the uncertainty it had created would have a long-term impact on the Premier League’s brand.“I want to think that it doesn’t, but I don’t know,” he said. “Uncertainty is not in our control and our control is to bring everything that we can individually through the club to maintain the position that we have to be the best league in the world.”Arteta added: “The thing is that this has been going for various years. That process is still not finished. So it is very difficult to express how I feel, because it is not resolved. When it is resolved I can talk with clarity and tell you exactly how I feel.”It is understood Arsenal and other Premier League clubs are keen for the situation to be resolved as quickly as possible, although City’s appeal means it could drag on until at least the new year. Arteta also dismissed suggestions Arsenal could be the main beneficiaries should City find themselves relegated, having finished as runners up to them three years in a row before becoming champions last season.“I think we control our accelerator, and believe me, for seven years it’s been full gas in everything that we can do and take in every corner at maximum speed,” he said.Ed Aarons5.De Zerbi: my problem is being bottom, not CityRoberto De Zerbi insists he has no time to dwell on Manchester City’s guilty verdict with Tottenham bottom of the table. De Zerbi was a Napoli player when they faced Juventus in the 2006-07 season after Juve were found guilty of match-fixing and relegated to Serie B.Juventus had an initial 30-point deduction reduced to nine and still won promotion straight back to Serie A. Asked what the experience was like, De Zerbi replied: “I was crazy as a player, I don’t remember my thoughts, just think on the ball, just think on our job.“When you are a player, you don’t think too much. When you are a coach, the same because the focus is on your players, especially now because we are on the bottom of the table. I have no time to think of the other problems than my team, my club.”The Spurs manager said the scandal did not change Italian football, and added: “There are the people who have to decide to take the decision, with responsibility, with courage, and honesty, always. It’s not my job. My job is to be a coach. But I love respecting the rules, like all people in our club.”Dejan Kulusevski is on the verge of returning after more than 500 days out with a complex knee injury. The forward will travel to Manchester for Sunday’s crunch match against United to support the team as he closes in on a comeback.De Zerbi told his squad in a meeting that Kulusevski had set an example to them. “He’s an inspiration,” he said. “He reacted very well, with character, with courage, with passion.”De Zerbi said the first week of the three-week international break had been particularly “tough” and that he suffered “a lot”. The 47-year-old took a short holiday but was unable to switch off.“If you work with passion and work like me, you can’t go home and forget your work, especially in this type of moment – it’s inside you,” he said.He believes Spurs can replicate Aston Villa, who failed to win any of their first five Premier League games last season before winning 12 of their next 13 and qualifying for the Champions League.“It’s possible. Why not? But to do what Villa did, we have to click. But I think the first win is not a gift from God. You have to deserve to win. And we didn’t deserve to win so far.”Sam CunninghamExplore more on these topicsManchester CityThe talkManchester UnitedMichael CarrickLiverpoolAndoni IraolaVincent KompanyArsenalnewsShareReuse this content

title: West Ham’s penalty pain costs them top spot in Championship after QPR draw | Championship | The Guardian
description: The Hammers were unable to leapfrog back to the top of the Championship after a 1-1 London derby draw with QPR
Author: Guardian staff reporter
Headline: The Hammers were unable to leapfrog back to the top of the Championship after a 1-1 London derby draw with QPR
Content: Pierce Charles makes the first of a dramatic double save to deny Jarrod Bowen from the spot in added time.Photograph: Justin Setterfield/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenPierce Charles makes the first of a dramatic double save to deny Jarrod Bowen from the spot in added time.Photograph: Justin Setterfield/Getty ImagesChampionshipWest Ham’s penalty pain costs them top spot in Championship after QPR drawPress AssociationFri 9 Oct 2026 17.19 EDTLast modified on Fri 9 Oct 2026 19.27 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe QPR goalkeeper Pierce Charles made a stunning double save from a Jarrod Bowen penalty in stoppage time to secure a 1-1 draw at West Ham. The 21-year-old, who kept four clean sheets and saved a penalty for Northern Ireland over the international break, pulled off more heroics to deny the Hammers top spot in theChampionship.Bowen had already equalised for West Ham, cancelling out a hugely controversial first-half penalty from Nicolas Madsen. But the Hammers captain saw his spot-kick saved and Charles then somehow pushed the rebound from Arne Engels on to the crossbar.West Ham were earlier on the wrong end of a dreadful penalty decision after Tomas Soucek was penalised for fouling Paul Smyth. Replays showed the challenge was well outside the area and that the Hammers midfielder got the ball. A VAR review would have definitely overturned referee Ruebyn Ricardo’s decision but with no technology in the Championship it stood, to the dismay of the majority inside the London Stadium.The West Ham assistant coach Rui Pedro Silva was booked for his complaints, as was Engels for stamping on the penalty spot, but Madsen kept his cool and calmly rolled the ball into the bottom corner.View image in fullscreenNicolas Madsen celebrates after rolling home from the spot.Photograph: John Walton/PARangers almost doubled their lead from a West Ham corner, mounting a swift counterattack which left recalled striker Rayan Kolli with a shooting opportunity 15 yards out, but Mads Hermansen made a fine save.Just as he had done at Millwall last time out with his side 2-0 down, the West Ham manager, Nuno Espírito Santo, made a double substitution at half-time, sending on Pablo Felipe and Edvin Austbø for Soucek and Kyle Walker-Peters. But Rangers almost struck again when Smyth danced past Konstantinos Mavropanos and into the area, only for the Greek defender to make a crucial recovery tackle.View image in fullscreenA tribute to former West Ham goalkeeper Ludek Miklosko, who died in September, at the game.Photograph: John Walton/PABowen, well marshalled by Rangers left-back Boy Kemper, had been enduring a frustrating evening until he burst into life in the 70th minute. The England international won the ball back with a crunching tackle on Ronnie Edwards, earning himself a bloody nose in the process. Pablo played the ball back to Bowen, who darted into the area and saw his first shot block before snaffling the rebound.View image in fullscreenJarrod Bowen after levelling for the Hammers.Photograph: John Walton/PAWest Ham went in search of a winner and Bowen’s scuffed effort looked destined for the net until Charles flung out a hand to push it past a post. Then, as the clock ticked into stoppage time Rangers substitute Amadou Mbengue grabbed a handful of Pablo’s shirt, referee Ricardo pointed to the spot again, but Charles superbly denied Bowen and Engels to earn his side a point.Explore more on these topicsChampionshipWest Ham UnitedQPRmatch reportsShareReuse this content

title: Chelsea manager Alonso insists Cole Palmer is committed to playing for England  | Chelsea | The Guardian
description: Xabi Alonso has said Cole Palmer is committed to playing for England despite missing England’s most recent matches across the international window
Author: Jacob Steinberg
Headline: Xabi Alonso has said Cole Palmer is committed to playing for England despite missing England’s most recent matches across the international window
Content: Cole Palmer missed the four England matches over the last fortnight.Photograph: Dave Shopland/APView image in fullscreenCole Palmer missed the four England matches over the last fortnight.Photograph: Dave Shopland/APChelseaChelsea manager Alonso insists Cole Palmer is committed to playing for EnglandPalmer pulled out of England squad due to injuryAttacker available for Chelsea’s game with BournemouthJacob SteinbergFri 9 Oct 2026 17.30 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleXabi Alonso has said Cole Palmer is committed to playing for England and revealed Chelsea’s No 10 missed this international break with a problem related to the groin injury that kept him out for much of last season.Thomas Tucheldid not hide his disappointmentwith Palmer, who is fit to face Bournemouth on Saturday, after the attacker made himself unavailable for the start of his country’s Nations League campaign last month. Tuchel said the 24-year-old “misses too many opportunities” to play for England and questioned whether Palmer wanted to be part of the squad.European FAs pushing for three-week international break to be abandonedRead morePalmer has won five caps sincescoring against Spain in the Euro 2024 finalbut his latest withdrawal was for genuine reasons. Palmer struggled with persistent groin pain last season, which led to him missing out on a place in Tuchel’s World Cup squad, and felt minor irritation beforeChelsea’s defeat by Brentfordlast month. It still needs careful management, and Alonso is adamant Chelsea’s talisman is intent on playing for England.“The most important thing for Cole is to be fully fit, that he enjoys his game, that he is feeling OK,” Chelsea’s manager said. “Whenever he is not, like in the Brentford game, we could see that he was struggling. He’s committed but he needs to be fully fit to play. We need him – the club and the national team.”The recent issue is nowhere as near as bad as when Palmer struggled to shoot properly last season. Resting during the extended break has helped. “Now he’s fine,” Alonso said. “He’s been feeling better this week. We use the first two weeks for him to recover. It’s a little bit from the pubalgia he had.”Tuchel has plenty of competition in attacking midfield and it remains to be seen whether he picks Palmer for next month’s games against Croatia and Spain. Alonso was asked whether a player can be considered truly world class if they do not play international football. “Things happen naturally,” he said. “When you show for your club that you are a top-level player and you have regularity, normally it is the natural way that you are part of the national team.”Alonso was nonplussed to hear about the broadcaster Piers Morgan calling Palmer a bottle job for failing to represent England. “I don’t know the comment and I don’t know the guy,” he said.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionPalmer has been in fine form for Chelsea this season, scoring four goals. They will need him at his best after three league games without a win. Alonso hopes that Reece James, Moisés Caicedo and Marco Palestra will also return from injury against Bournemouth.Explore more on these topicsChelseaXabi AlonsonewsShareReuse this content

title: Manchester United’s early wobble makes Tottenham visit a must-win for Carrick | Manchester United | The Guardian
description: After a scratchy start in the league, injuries and an underwhelming Rashford, Spurs’s visit to Old Trafford is already crucial for the hosts
Author: Will Unwin
Headline: After a scratchy start in the league, injuries and an underwhelming Rashford, Spurs’s visit to Old Trafford is already crucial for the hosts
Content: Marcus Rashford, here against Fulham just before the international break, has not had a goal involvement this season.Photograph: Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenMarcus Rashford, here against Fulham just before the international break, has not had a goal involvement this season.Photograph: Marc Atkins/Getty ImagesManchester UnitedManchester United’s early wobble makes Tottenham visit a must-win for CarrickAfter a scratchy start in the league, injuries and an underwhelming Rashford, Spurs’s visit to Old Trafford is already crucial for the hostsWill UnwinFri 9 Oct 2026 11.10 EDTLast modified on Fri 9 Oct 2026 11.27 EDTSharePrefer the Guardian on GoogleThe noise in the Premier League was focused elsewhere for the last two weeks of the international break, allowing a glorious silence to drift across Manchester United.Without Manchester City’s woes, Michael Carrick may have faced a more difficult time, with plenty to review in regards to the first five games of the season.Unitedsit solemnly in 12thwith only one league win, and misery needs company. The hosts will find just that at Old Trafford on Saturday evening. Tottenham, bottom of the Premier League, visit, with both sides hoping to kickstart their season. Spurs havesecured a measly two pointsafter a summerwhere £300m was spenton Roberto De Zerbi’s rebuild but the architect’s drawings are already at risk of being set alight. For Carrick and United, beating the worst team in the league is close to a necessity as they enter a very difficult run of fixtures.Will Carlos Baleba fix Manchester United? Three big questions ahead of potential debutRead moreOctober is theoretically and practically problematic for United, who have six fixtures this month, with away games against Leeds, Atlético Madrid, Como and Chelsea, who play a variety of styles that need preparing for, making a home game against Spurs a must-win. On paper, the second easiest game of the month is Bournemouth at home. Carrick has plenty of credit in the bank from his work in the second half of last season, and will be afforded as much time as possible to get things right because no one is eager for another mid-season change of manager. United need to be in a better position by the end of October than they started it, which will require significant improvement on the pitch.For Carrick there are plenty of small margins he can point to. The opening-day defeat at Hull was a grisly performance and worthy of criticism; Ipswich were eventually dispatched, whilethe derby was a tight and controversial loss, coming between two draws. The truth of the matter is United know they need to be better in both boxes. United have conceded fewer opposition touches in their box than any other team in the league but, on the other hand, they are the only side yet to keep a clean sheet. They can also boast the most touches in opposition boxes but are largely incapable of killing matches off.United, like Tottenham, are very good at dominating possession, averaging 60% per match, but cannot translate that to goals and points. Even in the victory against Ipswich, United were unable to put a full 90 minutes of composure together, relying on Bruno Fernandes to drag them through against a promoted side. The forwards are yet to synchronise, with Matheus Cunha, the man tasked with leading the line, having only one goal to his name, and even that took a heavy deflection.No one has more than one assist so far, while only Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo have scored twice or more, thePortuguese getting a hat-trickagainst Ipswich. Marcus Rashford has shown glimpses of promise on the left but has no goal involvements, giving the impression of a man who requires a confidence boost after returning to the club where he was not wanted for 18 months. Nor is there the option of Benjamin Sesko playing as a more traditional central striker given he is sidelined with injury, while Joshua Zirkzee cannot even class himself as a plan B. But United are prolific compared with Tottenham, whose only league goals came in a 3-2 defeat by Aston Villa just before the international break.View image in fullscreenMichael Carrick has had lots to ponder this season, with only one league win so far.Photograph: Bradley Collyer/PALosing to 10-man Manchester City was the most worrying of United’s defeats, showing how far off they look against a Champions League side. Phil Foden’s red card gave United plenty of space but they were unable to take advantage, instead plodding around, short of ideas, barely threatening. United are expert at dominating possession but not games, traits that create hope and frustration in equal measure.The summer signings of a goalkeeper who cost nothing and three central midfielders is coming under as much scrutiny as Carrick’s tactics. At least Carlos Baleba is poised to finally make his debut after joining from Brighton for £65m in August and Carrick desperately needs him to provide the energy lacking in central areas thus far. Having recovered from an ankle injury, the Cameroonian has what it takes to snuff out the danger that has been leading to the concession of goals.skip past newsletter promotionFree newsletter |Every weekdaySign up toFootball DailyKick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of footballEnter your emailSign upafter newsletter promotionSesko is not the sole injury concern; Kobbie Mainoo and Marcus Rashford were ruled out of playing for England, while Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui’s international breaks ended prematurely. Meanwhile, Matthijs de Ligt has not played competitively for 10 months and Amad Diallo is yet to feature this season.The run of 12 wins in 17 games after Carrick took interim charge in January showed plenty of individual and collective improvements, but whether certain players can crash through their current ceiling requires clear evidence sooner rather than later. With finances tight, it is imperative that United improve from within. More academy players have spent time with the squad in recent weeks, with Noah Ajayi impressing the coaches Steve Holland and Jonathan Woodgate. It is thought a number of youngsters could make first-team debuts before the season concludes, which would be a display of Carrick’s long-term vision. Results, however, will decide if he gets a chance to implement it in the first place.United are desperate for a catalyst and if it does not come against Tottenham at the weekend, Carrick will become fearful of Halloween.Explore more on these topicsManchester UnitedfeaturesShareReuse this content

title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers | Premier League | The Guardian
description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and once-reliable forwards underperform against xG
Author: Andrew Beasley
Headline: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and once-reliable forwards underperform against xG
Content: Only two teams in the top flight have scored fewer goals than expected this season than James Maddison’s Spurs.Photograph: Alex Pantling/Getty ImagesView image in fullscreenOnly two teams in the top flight have scored fewer goals than expected this season than James Maddison’s Spurs.Photograph: Alex Pantling/Getty ImagesPremier LeagueAnalysisThe Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointersAndrew BeasleyGoal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xGFri 9 Oct 2026 14.00 EDTLast modified on Fri 9 Oct 2026 14.02 EDTShareGoals are on the up in thePremier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste.If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark.Chart showing goals and expected goals per game in the Premier League since 2021-22This is an issue across the Premier League. Fourteen clubs have scored fewer goals than expected, whether penalties are included or not, up from 10 last season. While there are eight teams that are within a goal of their underlying numbers and may see an immediate change of fortunes this weekend, the remaining 12 are split 8-4 towards the underachievers.It is not just season-wide averages that are crumbling but week-by-week performances, too. There were 24 instances of a team scoring at least one goal fewer than their xG implied they should have across the first five match weeks, twice as many as occurred in the opening 50 games last season.There are numerous possible explanations. Chance quality does not appear to be one of them, as the expected goals per non-penalty shot average only drops once more decimal places are applied than feels healthy.Chart showing goals minus expected goals in the 2026-27 Premier LeagueAt first glance, volume of touches in the penalty area has barely shifted either. A Premier League team is averaging 24.8 touches in the opposition box per game, down just 0.6 on last season.The breakdown by team is more revealing. Four of last season’s top five are having fewer box touches per match, with Aston Villa and Liverpool having seen around a third disappear from their averages.The one team from the quintet to increase is Manchester United, but they have only played one club that finished in the top 10 last season and five of their eight goalsoccurred against Championship runners-up Ipswich. A finely tuned attacking machine they are not. United top the Premier League for non-penalty shots, and are joint-second bottom for the average expected goal value.They have not been helped by their top player for non-penalty xG: Bryan Mbeumo is one of 10 players who have scored at least one goal fewer than underlying numbers imply he should have. As he underachieved by 1.19 last season, this is not especially odd. The issue is how reliant United are upon the 27-year-old. This problem is not exclusive to this combination of club and player either.Chart showing each team’s leading player for expected goals in 2026‑27The top player for expected goals at almost every Premier League club is having a bigger share of the xG pie than they enjoyed last season. This need not necessarily be a concern, as the figures will drop once playing time and chances are more equally shared within squads.The most involved players themselves may help explain why goals are down, though. The top players from each club have collectively scored 6.8 non-penalty goals fewer than expected, almost 40% of the shortfall across the division from just 20 players.Thierno Barry has been the player taking the chance for 49.4% of Everton’s non-penalty expected goals this season, up from 17.7% last term. It’s a massive increase in responsibility for a relatively young player – he has scored twice from chances valued at 3.5 xG.Alexander Isak has seen a greater leap in share of team expected goals, though injuries meant he did not feature that often last season. There are seeds of growth for him at Liverpool, but he remains relatively new in terms of minutes played for the club. As with more than half of Premier League clubs, Isak is playing under a new man in the dugout.Isak’s replacement at Newcastle, Yoanne Wissa, underperformed against xG by more than two goals last season, as did Marcus Tavernier at Bournemouth. They may not be the best players for their clubs to funnel their chances through. At least they are preferable to the situation at Tottenham, where centre-back Jan Paul van Hecke is their leading player for non-penalty expected goals.Elsewhere, the players with the most xG for Fulham (Gonzalo García) and Ipswich (Emersonn) are 22 years old and new to English football. Hull’s Oli McBurnie, meanwhile, has never scored more than six goals in a Premier League campaign. Erling Haaland remains a reliable presence in the xG-heavy frontman stakes, but the situation at Manchester City may affect his form.Excessive reliance on players who can be forgiven for underperforming could prove to be a small-sample statistical quirk that is quickly remedied. Until it is, do not bank on the goal rate reaching the expected goal level in the Premier League.Explore more on these topicsPremier LeagueanalysisShareReuse this content

title: Premier League team news: predicted lineups for the weekend action | Soccer | The Guardian
description: Manchester City travel to Liverpool after a trying international break while struggling Tottenham aim to turn things around at Old Trafford
Author: Guardian sport
